summary.text: Allen Miller is the Democratic candidate for the Indiana House of Representatives, District 73, in the November 3, 2026 general election, facing Republican incumbent Jennifer Meltzer.
A technical writer who lives in Greensburg, he lists infrastructure, workers' rights and public education among his priorities.

paragraphs.text: Allen Miller graduated from Cardinal Ritter High School and earned a bachelor's degree from the Franciscan University of Steubenville in 2014.
His career experience includes working as a technical writer.
In a Ballotpedia survey, he said he was born and raised in Indiana, lived on a small farm outside Pendleton as a child, moved to Indianapolis at age 7, and settled in Greensburg in 2018.
He said he is the father of two children.
Miller advanced from the Democratic primary for District 73 on May 5, 2026, without a primary opponent.

In his survey, he said the state's biggest hurdle is abandoned infrastructure, including roads, stormwater systems, bridges and public transit, and that he wants public utility infrastructure reclaimed from private interests.
He said he would work to repeal Indiana's right-to-work law, strengthen unions and raise the minimum wage.
He also said he supports restoring school district funding that he said Senate Bill 1 reduced and ending the school choice program, which he called a "scam."
